title: Skeletal System: Skull & Bones
attribution: Adapted from OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e, Section 7.2 (CC BY 4.0). Access for free at openstax.org.

labels.definition: Forms the forehead and the roof of the orbits. Contains the air-filled frontal sinus.
Paired bones forming most of the superior and lateral walls of the cranium. Meet at the sagittal suture.
Form the lower lateral skull. House the middle and inner ear; include the mastoid process and the jaw-joint fossa.
Forms the back and base of the skull. Contains the foramen magnum, where the spinal cord exits.
Butterfly-shaped keystone bone of the central skull base. Its sella turcica cradles the pituitary gland.
Delicate bone between the eyes forming the nasal roof and part of the septum. Its cribriform plate passes the olfactory nerves.
Fused upper jaw bones. Hold the upper teeth and form the anterior hard palate and parts of the orbits and nose.
The cheekbones. Form the lateral cheek and orbital margin; part of the zygomatic arch.
Two small bones forming the bridge of the nose, anchoring the nasal cartilages.
Smallest facial bones, in the medial orbit. Help form the canal that drains tears to the nasal cavity.
Form the posterior hard palate and part of the nasal wall, separating the oral and nasal cavities.
Paired curved bones on the lateral nasal walls that warm, moisten, and filter inhaled air.
Slender midline bone forming the inferior, posterior part of the nasal septum.
The lower jaw — the only moveable skull bone. Articulates with the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint (TMJ).

keyTerms.definition: The portion of the skull that encloses and protects the brain (8 brain-case bones).
An immobile fibrous joint between adjacent skull bones (coronal, sagittal, lambdoid, squamous).
Large opening in the occipital bone through which the spinal cord exits the skull.
Saddle-shaped depression of the sphenoid bone that houses the pituitary gland.
Air-filled cavities (frontal, maxillary, sphenoid, ethmoid) that lighten the skull and warm/moisten air.
Weakest point of the skull where four bones meet at the temple; overlies the middle meningeal artery.

steps.prompt: The skull has 22 bones: 8 in the brain case and 14 facial bones. Let's tour the brain case first.
Tap each glowing bone to reveal its name and role. Explode the skull to separate the bones.
Find the foramen magnum on the occipital bone — the spinal cord passes through here.
The sphenoid is the keystone bone that touches every other cranial bone. Its sella turcica holds the pituitary.
Quick check: which bones contain paranasal sinuses?

steps.instruction: Select the ONLY moveable bone of the skull.
steps.hint: It forms the lower jaw and moves at the TMJ.

steps.instruction: Select the bone that contains the foramen magnum.
steps.hint: It's at the back and base of the skull.

steps.instruction: Select the butterfly-shaped keystone bone at the central skull base.
steps.hint: It cradles the pituitary gland in the sella turcica.
It forms the lateral cheek and part of the orbit.

steps.instruction: Select the bone that forms the forehead.
Reassemble the skull: place the mandible into its socket on the skull.
steps.hint: It hinges at the temporal bones.
